overview.title: The saga
overview.text:
Grandmother Naadag, an elder of the Diné Republic who had lived most of her life in Cahokia, chose the day of her own death and held a Seeing for it. The characters came to it by different roads. At its end she asked them, in a private meeting that was not recorded, to carry a box to Oraibi, in the Diné Republic. They leave Cahokia on the morning of the eleventh day with Syn asleep and shaking, and with no way to wake them. [SET]

The trip is a week, a week and a half with stops. Nothing about the delivery is urgent, and they are not trying to rush it. [SET — Notion] They navigate by a song map. [SET — session 1/C's recap] Daatsu navigates; Tika is hired as an escort and works with him. [SET — Notion]

*Naadag Hasaka* is Chahi for *Crow Mesa*: *Naadag*, crow; *Hasaka*, mesa. [SOURCE — the book's glossary]

overview.title: The Seeing
overview.text:
The Story Guide's invention for this saga [YOURS]. A Seeing is for a respected elder choosing their own death, and runs ten days:

- Days 1–2: arrivals, informal greetings, food, games. Nobody has to be there at the start.
- Days 3–4: the long tables — speeches, stories, the gift-giving and the feast (day 3); the life told by several storytellers, then speeches by leaders and elders (day 4).
- Days 5–6: the elder withdraws with one or two attendants to prepare; the guests are quieter, reflect, rest. The kitchens close.
- Day 7: the death at dawn, privately. The attendants take a blocker against the compound burned in the room; it stops the elder's body.
- Days 8–9: the body is viewed, then buried or cremated; mourning.
- Day 10: farewells and dispersal. Anyone not gone by the end of it is expected to be.

About two hundred people came to Grandmother's, counting children. Not everyone is given a Seeing; her husband Misyooyi's death, about fifteen years before, was quiet. (Soova's timeline puts it in 689; the 1/B session notes say about fifteen years, and the chronicle follows the notes.) The death is by smoke: a mixture of plants burned into a fume that slows and stops the body, trivially negated by the right medicine taken first. [SET — 1/C notes]

sections.title: The Black
sections.text: Everyone experiences the Black in their own way, and the same person may see it differently at different times. [SET] Syn: a translucent overlay on the world that darkens the deeper they go, until they lose where they are and stop hearing speech. Soova: a spirit body that moves while her senses are set aside, hazy until she focuses on a place. Migatuka: vivid, dreamlike, first person, and she reads it as her own subconscious rather than anything outside her. The Black is a rhizome: everything touches everything in another dimension, which is how some spooky action at a distance works. [SET — Notion]

sections.title: The wild corridor
sections.text: A broad north–south stripe of unoccupied territory, kept for animal migration, just before the Diné Republic; off limits by treaty. No one lives in it; you can cross it — "Burning Man ethos, leave the site"; a DMZ without the extreme penalties? Who is breaching the treaty? What it is called is a Notion GM question. Not in the book. [YOURS] [OPEN] (2/A notes; a map of it is on the 2/A page.)

sections.title: The way west
sections.text: From Cahokia to the destination by way of Coyote City: in our world's terms, Memphis to Albuquerque — down the Mississippi and up the Arkansas by water, then across the plains past the Wichita Mountains and the Caprock Escarpment, the Sangre de Cristo to the north, to the Rio Grande valley under the Sandias. On the plains: migratory caravans, solar-powered pop-up villages, buffalo ranchers, treeless grassland with trees only along the streams; circuit justice, gangs, the Suyata. [YOURS — 2/A notes]

sections.title: Getting around, keeping in touch
sections.text: Few wheeled vehicles; most things float or hover (yutsu barges), and there are paths more than roads. The daso is regional: Cahokia has its own, which interconnects with others in the Free Lands; the Diné Republic's is separate. There may be no wireless version — something more like sneakernet or carrier pigeon. A niisi on the wrist texts and reaches the local daso; a Diné niisi needs reworking to talk to Cahokia's. You always stop for someone on foot. [SET — sessions; Notion]

sections.title: Drink, and kelera root
sections.text: There is no alcohol culture. The everyday drinks are brewed from herbs and fungus, microdoses that even children take, like weak beer once was; stronger brews and distillations go up to "don't operate heavy machinery". [SET] Kelera root is the base of many of them: it raises blood flow, dulls pain, and is mildly hallucinogenic. Kelera-adanadi, the root the Adanadi has marked, is the nearest thing to a controlled substance: it cannot be grown reliably (growers make the conditions and hope; there is research into it), and for someone who already carries the Adanadi it has a resonance that heightens what they feel. Migatuka will not have regular access to it. [SET] Substances are not banned as such; someone who is a danger to themselves or others through use can be made to accept support. [SET]

sections.title: Food
sections.text: Vegetarianism exists; veganism does not really, since what it avoids mostly never came over or was never made. [SET]

sections.title: The year and the war
sections.text: 710 is the present. The All Tribes War ran 612–623. If Grandmother was 121, she was born in 589 and was 23 when the war began. The Diné Republic (Dinada) has a National Council, kivas and clans. [SET — Notion]

sections.title: Gambling with Naasi
sections.text:
One of my adversary NPC's has the Addiction (gambling) burden, and is going to secretly attempt to wager the evidence against the party that they are being hunted for against one of the PC's surrendering. As such, I made rules for using Naasii as a gambling game in Coyote and Crow proper:

Naasii is played between 2-4 players.

- All players agree on each player’s stake. Normally, this is an even nizi stake, but items and favors can also be wagered. All games of Naasii are winner-takes-all
- The game takes place over 2-5 rounds. Winner is the first person who wins two rounds.
- First roller is determined by a single D12 roll, the highest number goes first, play proceeds clockwise until all players have scored or busted that round. In the event of a tie on first player roll, players keep rolling until one rolls a higher number
- On their turn, the roller rolls 3 white dice. They are attempting to make runs (numbers in ascending order) or sets (instances of the same number). After rolling their dice, they have the option of scoring their dice or rolling again.

a. If they roll again, they lock at least one of their dice, then pick up their unlocked dice and reroll them. To that roll, they add 2 white dice and 1 black die. They then have the option of scoring or rolling a 3rd time. They can roll again after that a 4th and final time. Each time they roll, the reroll the unlocked dice and add 2 white and 1 black die. Any white die showing a 12 is wild

i. Characters may use Legendary Ranks and Mind to increase or decrease the value of any white die in any roll after black dice are resolved. White dice cannot be increased to a 12, and black dice cannot be affected

b. In rolls 2-4, before scoring or rolling again, each player must resolve their black dice. If any black die shows a 12, the player BUSTS and their turn ends with no points scored unless they also show a 12 among their unlocked dice. Otherwise, the player may not score one die matching their black die (but may score all but one die if multiple white dice show that number). A Bust may be avoided if the player has also rolled a white 12 to counter it.

i. An unscrupulous player may also attempt to cheat their way out of a Bust using a Skulduggery check. The SN is the highest Mental Defense of their opponents with the following modifiers:

1. +1 SN for each opponent beyond the first

2. +1 SN for every 3 neutral or opposed onlookers

a. Each +1 can be counteracted with a success from a simultaneous Charm or Deception as a distraction by an allied onlooker. A critical success may be used to remove a +1 from an opponent beyond the first, or give -1 SN if there are only 2 players

3. +1 SN for every other Bust a player has averted this game using this method

ii. On a success, the player may change their black die showing a 12 to match one of their unlocked white dice. On a critical success, they may change it to any number. On a failure, they still Bust. On a critical failure, the players attempt to cheat is discovered by their opponents.

- The winner of the round is the player who has the most dice scored as part of a set or run. In the case of a tie, each player rolls their unscored white dice again simultaneously and scores them to their run or set. Continue until one player has more scored dice than another.

a. If two or more players score a set or run of 9 dice, the round restarts with only those players participating

b. If all players before the final player in a round have busted, the last player may score a run or set of 1 on their first roll to win the round.

- In the situation that all players have won 1 round, the last round occurs simultaneously. All players roll at the same time, resolve any black dice, then secretly select one of their white or black dice that has yet to be rolled. They reveal the selected dice simultaneously. A white die designates that the player will score their dice, a black die designates that the player will roll again

a. In the case that all remaining players bust on the same roll during a simultaneous round, all dice in that roll are re-rolled.

- Sidebets are popular in games of Naasii as well. These are played in a pool system, and usually overseen by the house in gambling dens. Onlookers pay into a pool, usually a 10, 50, or 100 nizi buy-in, and are assigned a number. A tracker notes all numbers rolled every roll (if it matters, this occurs in the step after Legendary Ranks and Mind are assigned but before dice are scored/locked) and keeps a running tally. Numbers are divided as evenly as possible, and the pool is split evenly with the winners (or co-winners if two or more numbers are at the top). In professional gambling dens, it is customary for the house to always take 12 and no payout be awarded to patrons should 12 be the most common roll.

- ↳ Lose 1 Point indicates that the Player is continuing to worsen. They take a point of Damage in the appropriate category (Body, Mind, or Soul). If this reduces them to the point where they would die, see Death. Otherwise, they will continue to be Dying in the next Round.
- ↳ No change indicates that the Character is still in a Dying state and they will have to make another Check the following Round. There is no other effect.
- ↳ Stabilized indicates that the appropriate Stat (Body, Mind, or Soul) has stabilized, the Player does not have to make additional Checks in subsequent Rounds, and that they are no longer considered Dying if this was their only Derived Stat below zero. They do not gain or lose any more points unless they take Damage from a subsequent attack.
- ↳ If another Character spends a Primary Action to make a First Aid Check on a Dying Character and gets any Successes, the Character does not lose any Body points that Round. If the Character making the First Aid Check gets a Critical Success, the Character stabilizes and does not need further medical attention to keep from dying. If the Character attempting the Skill Check gets a Critical Failure, they do a point of Body Damage to the subject. It is important to note that First Aid only affects Body. Only a Dying Character can Stabilize themselves from loss of Mind and Soul

sections.title: Rest and Healing
sections.text:
There are five ways that a Character can regain lost Mind, Body, and Spirit:

- Various Skills (Medicine, Ceremony, etc)
- Abilities
- Drugs
- Short Rest
- Long Rest

Each Character in a Short Rest makes three Checks upon completion of the Short Rest; an Endurance Check, a Wisdom Check, and a Will Check. Every Success gained on those rolls returns one point of corresponding Body, Mind, and Spirit.

Short Rests can only be taken a maximum of twice a day, and can only be taken after an Encounter

A Long Rest allows for the regaining of Body, Mind and Spirit. A Character that has taken a Long Rest makes Checks, as with a Short Rest. In addition to the gains listed in a Short Rest, the Character taking a Long Rest also gains Body, Mind, and Soul points equal to their Endurance, Wisdom, and Will Stat.

Healing Stat Damage: see page 330

sections.title: Cost Ranks
sections.text:
1 = minimal

8 = astronomical

» Cost Rank < Wealth Rank = No Check needed, Character gets item automatically

» Cost Rank = Wealth Rank = Check (see below)

The form of Debt will be determined by the situation, but in general, Debts make it more difficult to make future Wealth Checks. Additionally, the Story Guide may make the Debt something beyond financial. The Character may owe favors to unsavory types or be made to do labor in exchange for goods or any other form of compensation that the Story Guide thinks fits the scenario.

people.title: Grandmother Naadag
people.text:
Nearly 121 at her death; born 589 in the Diné Republic. Orphaned at the end of the All Tribes War; the man who became her husband, Misyooyi, found her on his way back, and she came to Cahokia with him in her adolescence. "I have not been to Diné since I was a child." Misyooyi died about fifteen years before her; she lost children of her own. A portrait of her is on the site. Ceremonial more than spiritual. Honoured by the Council of Twelve for neighbourhood work copied across the city. Related to the Ancients in Oraibi. [SET — Notion; the recordings]

She knew Soova's past for many years and protected her, largely without Soova's knowledge, from the people who came to make her finish her work; she told Soova so before she died (in a letter, or in the last days — Notion leaves it open). [SET — Notion] Connected to the Coyote crime lords, as Soova and Syn are. [SET — Notion]

Her plan, from the 1/A GM notes: she understands she can no longer protect Soova from the crime family Soova escaped, so she sends the party into Dinada — for several reasons, one being to give Soova a clean slate, a pardon. Daatsu gets them there with a song map to an ancient city older than the Diné (their devices will not work inside Dinada). Syn and Tika are to be the left and right eyes. Migatuka is told to tend Soova's health; really it is a detox trip. In play (1/B) she gave Soova a sealed box to return to her ancestral lands, sang Daatsu the song map ("Thank you for guiding my daughter back home"), told Syn "I trust your sight", and asked Migatuka to bring Soova home safe and well — then told Soova alone that this was "only half true". [SET — Notion]

Notion GM questions: Was she Soova's great-aunt, and does Soova learn it? Why is sending Soova intended to be a pardon? What did she ask them to bring to Oraibi, and why? What did she give Syn? [OPEN]

The early part of her life, as the family tells it, has deliberate gaps. Syn came away convinced they concern Grandmother and the Black: something she met there and has been getting away from, dangerous enough that it is better not to know there is anything to avoid. That reading came from a critical failure and may be wrong. Who reached Syn through the Black with the family's name is not established. [OPEN]

sections.title: Walk The Black
sections.text:
Activation: 1 point of Mind, 1 point of Soul

Dice Check: Will Walk the Black allows a person to leave their body and move around in a spirit or astral form, staying either in the physical world or traversing over to The Black. Doing this takes focus and concentration and can only be done outside of an Encounter. While the user is out of their body, their physical form is motionless and considered Unconscious. To Activate the Ability, the Character sits or lies down, and spends a point of Mind and a point of Soul. They then make a Will Check. A Success indicates they have successfully Activated the Ability. When the consciousness leaves the body, the Player decides whether they stay in reality or traverse to The Black. If they choose to keep their essence in reality, the Character makes a Charisma check. Every Success allows the Character access to one sense of the Player’s Choice. If the Character gets six or more Successes, they may receive supernatural sensory input (see Hawk's Eye). Staying in reality in this form requires total focus and every hour the Character must make another Charisma Check, choose their senses again, and spend a further point of Soul and Mind.

While in this form, they can travel unseen or heard and are entirely incorporeal. However, they can still be detected with five or more Successes on a Perception Check from another person. The Character cannot interact with the real world except to receive sensory input. They can move at no more than a slow walking speed and can pass through walls, floors, or any physical substance. Their essence cannot take Body Damage, but may take Mind or Spiritual Damage.

Alternatively, the Character may choose to travel to The Black. In this scenario, their essence leaves this plane and travels to a different realm of reality. For more on The Black, see the Chapter “Playing Coyote & Crow.

sections.text:
Activation: Secondary Action, 1 point of Mind

Dice Check: None With this Ability your Character may alter the way their own body behaves, down to the cellular level — it can change everything from heart rate to organ function to musculature. Activating this Ability costs a Secondary Action and 1 point of Mind. It may be used in or out of an Encounter. The Character may add one die to any roll involving a chosen Physical or Mental Stat for that Round (Strength, Agility, Endurance, Intelligence, Perception, Wisdom). This doesn't change their Stat nor does it affect Derived Stats, it simply adds one die to their Pool for that roll.

In addition, your Character can use this Ability to modify their physiology. There are a wide variety of uses for this but here are a few examples:

The Makokamit

The Makokamit people live between Cahokia and the Paha and are primarily occupied with animal

husbandry, particularly buffalo, antelope, and turkey. The Makokamit have as close a relationship with their various animals as the Nahoonak have with their plants.

They are also notable cooks. Because of the necessity of managing large herds of animals, the

Makokamit also excel in the production of personal transport vehicles. Theirs is the most rural of the Freelands city-states with the

most widely dispersed population.

Unlike the other nations, they tend to spend brief rotations living in the city portion of their city

state. Their government would be considered democratic, but without an authority compelling compliance to group decisions as long as they don’t affect the whole.

The Makokamit are more male-dominated than most Freeland people, particularly compared to

their neighbors the Paha. The Makokamit are also committed gamblers and considered the most oisterous of the Free Lands people. Although the Makokamit are considered somewhat coarse by their Paha neighbors, this is objectively an unfair characterization, as the Makokamit are keenly interested in fashion and personal ornamentation as well as music and

dancing. The Makokamit are nothing if not flashy.

Still low key. Not really meals, but there’s a trickle of food all day.

Daatsu is oblivious that the woman, Ninosh, he recommended mushroom steaks to keeps coming around and flirting with him, mentions her cooking, very interested in the provenance of the food. Migatuka overhears, and eventually just calls out (slightly buzzed on medicine and a microdose drink) “SHE WANTS TO FUCK YOU.”

The woman turns to Migatuka and laughs. “Was I that obvious?”

Migatuka: “Oh, honey.”

Ninosh blushes, and turns back to Daatsu. “Seek me out if you’re so inclined,” and makes her exit.

Migatuka runs into her colleague, Kaptaanzi. They never really got along.

Migatuka: “Hey, bitch, how’s medical?”

Kaptaanzi: “Better, recently.”

Migatuka: “I’m glad I’m not there.”

Kaptaanzi, judgy: “I can see why. I guess we shouldn’t be expecting you back anytime soon. Don’t worry about it, we’re good.”

Wazawi is glad to have completed her adulthood ritual, but feels out of place both with the kids and adults, and ends up going out into the woods of the big park. She takes advantage of her newfound privileges and camps out under the stars, not asking or telling anyone else what she’s doing.

Tomorrow they’ll begin speeches, and it’ll be more structured; today, with the chaos and lack of structure, Wazawi found it stressful.

Syn ends up being pulled into a game of naasi, blows on the dice to give the uncles luck.

Soova is a little irritated that Wazawi disappeared. She makes her final preparations, as the next couple days won’t allow her. Kooyoopi’s materials are already carefully set out. She then goes to bed.

**Seeing, Day 3**

Wazawi arrived, tried to help out. Very interested.

Late morning start. Tables gathered together, into roughly a U-shape. Grandmother is in the center, flanked by immediate family. At various points people stand up and give a speech, or an anecdote, or tell a funny story. Tawihichik, from the Council of Twelve, comes for a few hours and speaks of Naadag’s positive influence in the community.

Soova stands and tells of how meaningful it has been to learn from her; how to raise children. How to honor feelings without having them dictate one’s actions.

There’s a break for a rest/nap mid-afternoon, and there will be a feast in the evening. Daatsu gets pulled in to help prep.

Before the feast is a gift-giving. Syn and Daatsu are giving small handmade trinkets.

Migatuka is given a folded up blanket. She unfolds it and bursts into tears, hugging it close. It used to be Zibizin’s, and her falcon is still prominent, but it’s been amended to appear like a fox. Syn sees this and comes over to comfort. She goes and puts it in the cubby where her things are.

Soova gets a wooden case, which she opens and it is a beautiful jewelry set; an heirloom, and one that would have gone Naadag’s daughter, had she had one. Soova would never have presumed, but this cements the feeling of acceptance and integration into the family that she’s felt.

Soova: “Would it be okay if I wore these during your ceremonies?”

Grandmother: “I would be honored if you would.”

Soova: “I can’t tell you how much this means to me.”

They enjoy the food, the smoked eggs. Nothing starts until tomorrow afternoon, so that everyone can sleep late.

**Seeing, Day 4**

Once things get rolling, there’s something of a tag-teamed oral biography of Grandmother Naadag, with three or four storytellers passing the ball between them. The descriptions of her childhood are sparse and vague, and slightly cryptic. In adolescence she arrived with her now-husband in Cahokia. He died about 15 years ago. His death was a more muted affair.

It’s obvious to Syn that there’s an omission, but gets a [failed roll] strong feeling that it is something that feels too unsafe even to mention; that she experienced something in her relationship to the black, the void, that she is seeking to escape, or hide.

Then there’s a series of speeches.

Soova gives a speech about how Grandmother Naadag’s lost child helped her with the loss of her child, how not to get lost in grief.

Wazawi: this is the first seeing that she’s been present for this portion of. Listening intently. The early parts of the narrative feel weird, relatable but also hard to picture, especially since it was nearly 100 years ago.

They go out to watch the sun set, and then Grandmother Naadag retreats.

The evening ends in more quiet conversations, as small groups peel off, build fires, etc.

Wazawi asks Soova if she can participate or watch the next few days. Soova chides her, explains that she can be of assistances afterwards only.

Each gets sought out at a certain point, and told that Grandmother Naadag wishes to speak with them.

They gather around, a little confused. Fur curtains part as grandmother enters.

“Thank you. I have a request I ask of you. It is not something that can be done alone, which is why I ask this of all of you.”

She grasps Syn’s hands. “We have only just met, but you have the eyes that can see what needs to be seen, but the understanding will come from others. I trust your sight.”

She moves to Soova, and clasps her hands: “Like you, I do not come from Cahokia originally. Few know that, during the All-Tribes War, my husband found me on his way back. I have not been to Dine since I was a child, but I have something that I need returned to my ancestral lands.” She turns and hands Soova a sealed box. “I ask that after I am gone you would bring this back to its home.”

Turning to Daatsu, she says, “Your family speaks highly of you, and have consented to loaning you to me. Your skills are highly praised. I have a song for you.” And she proceeds to sing what is an antiquated song-map. Typically used for traversing large swathes of plain. At the refrain, when it begins to repeat, Daatsu join in. As they finish, she says, “Thank you for guiding my daughter back home.”

She gets to Migatuka. “Soova will need a healer. She can heal others, but she must not neglect herself. You are to make sure she is able to return in safety and health. Would you do that for me?” Migatuka agrees.

Everyone but Soova is dismissed.

Syn does not want anything to do with the box. Feels it is dangerous, or sacred.

Daatsu feels like it’s just cargo, but the song map; it goes farther west than he’s ever been, deep into the Dine Republic. It’s a complication he’s never dealt with before. Song maps are antiquated, haven’t been used in a generation or two; it’s unusual that he knows them.

Grandmother: “What I told Migatuka is only half true. She is struggling, and needs a healer of the soul. Time to recuperate, and space away from temptations, may be of help to her. I hope you two can be of aid to one another.”

Wazawi sneaks in, determinedly, and hides in a closet overnight, sleeping standing up, so as to be present in the morning. [massive stealth success]

Cooking, cybernetics with adanadi.

She was catering a portion of the Seeing. Tika came in to assist for a bit.

Tika gets embroiled in a conversation with someone who is hears their theories about reproducing the adanadi’s effects synthetically; they (Choyan) are skeptical. They talk through why they think that won’t work, and expose Tika to the more academic sources.

Tika gets shut out of some of the naasi games with the uncles. But the sports betting with favors is pretty typical.

Tika’s bet wins well, he ends up winning a job servicing a yutsu heading west. Paid 1/3 up front. Also will cook.

Migatuka is really feeling the loss of Zibizin, the loss of her miscarriage, the incoming loss of Naadag. She begins to have a vision. She sees her ‘spiritual’ experiences as manifesting from her subconscious. She feels herself looking through someone’s eyes, her eyes. She’s humming a tune. There’s a pot for kelera tea. She pours the hot tea into a drinking bowl. It’s far too large. There’s a voice from the other room, which sounds familiar, she can’t make it out. She looks back, and there’s an infant, presumably her child, under the water as the tea keeps pouring in. It starts to come up for air. She throws away the pot, turns back and the bowl is empty. She wakes up from the trip, sweating, it was really intense.

Migatuka was in a room with others sleeping, reading quietly, meditating, and she wakes with a start. Tries to keep her distress to herself, unsuccessfully. The others clearly notice but pretend like they don’t.

Soova and her assistant ready Grandmother Naadag. Massages, sage, trimming nails, braiding hair. Song plays a prominent role. There are namings of spirits, of ancestors, as guides.

Soova was anxious about all of this, but all of that prep pays off, it feels pretty natural. She is honored by the level of trust Grandmother Naadag is placing in her. It’s an emotional marathon, being so close to someone facing death in such a real way.

Towards the end of day six, Soova notices the door is ajar. The sleep is punctuated, vigil is held. Soova closes it, makes a note to ask about it.

The method of death is burning a combination of plants that produce an incredibly toxic and fatal smoke, but it’s trivially negated with appropriate medicine. It will slow and then stop Grandmother’s physical processes.

Tika tries showing off a kind of martial art in the park, sparring with others, but clearly can’t hold his own.

Soova is wearing the jewelry for the day of death. Senses something off. Uses Walk the Black to get a sense if there’s a bad spirit or something that might compromise the ritual. Has a sense of auras, but can interact slightly. Presses her sense forward, can see an outline of an aura, almost infrared, in the closet. Her astral body moves into the closet, and she finds Wazawi, body sore and tensed, trying to stretch some muscles individually. Trying to stay awake, struggling, can’t sleep.

Soova is mad. Big mad. She also knows that if she hadn’t found her it would’ve been fatal.

As she returns to her body, she plays things out in her head; she can’t compromise the ceremony. It would dishonor the family to reveal the situation, but she’s willing to accept that, but the ceremony is more important.

Soova goes and prepares the antidote, and opens the closet to a stupored Wazawi. In an urgent whisper, she gives Wazawi the medicine and scolds her for how unacceptable this was, and that she will stay in the closet until everything is finished. She gives Wazawi some water and closes the closet again.

Wazawi is too exhausted to have any will to fight, and meekly complies.

At dawn, Soova wakes her assistant and Grandmother, and they greet the dawn one last time, before settling in holding hands as the tendrils of smoke begin to fill the room. Soova reassures grandmother.

She can feel her sweat, she sings fragments of melodies that feel nostalgic to Soova from her childhood.

When the life leaves the body, they dress the body one last time in preparation for viewing and burial, and then Soova sneaks Wazawi out, and then sleeps for the remainder of the day and night.

During the viewing, Migatuka has the blanket around her shoulders, and some kelera tea.

Afterward, the group spends the next couple days gathering necessary materials. Daatsu finds a yutsu bus to take westward, and Tika is the support personnel.

Soova is upset but also knows she has very little time to get a lot together.

Tika is a decent pilot, but hasn’t done rural travel much.

Daatsu is thinking “if I had known, I would have brought x, and y, and z….”

They found Syn in her room, comatose, shaking. Soova recognizes that this isn’t medical, they bring her along and Soova and Migatuka mind her.
